context.product: Fernway Learn, an online platform with AI skills courses and an AI tutor
context.audience: Working professionals moving into AI roles

screens.retrievalDescription: A minimalist desktop landing page hero section for Fernway Learn set against a clean off-white background with a pale lavender and cyan radial gradient. The top navigation bar displays the 'Fernway Learn' brand wordmark on the far left, middle navigation links 'Courses', 'Paths', 'Pricing', and 'Blog', and small control icons on the far right. The left column of the hero features bold dark navy headline text 'Master AI skills that get you hired' with 'AI skills' highlighted in periwinkle. Accompanying body copy reads: 'Bite-sized courses, hands-on projects and an AI tutor that adapts to you. Join thousands of learners building real careers.' Below the copy are a rounded periwinkle primary button labeled 'Get Started' and a subtle text link 'Learn more'. To the right floats an elevated white card with soft drop shadows titled 'Your learning path', displaying skeleton placeholder bars representing learning modules. Below the hero section, a horizontal grid presents four white metric cards: '120+ Courses', '50k Learners', '4.8 Average rating', and '92% Completion', followed by the microcopy 'Trusted by teams at leading companies worldwide'.

A centered mobile or desktop web registration modal for Fernway set on a white card background. At the top, the 'Fernway' wordmark appears in vibrant purple on the left, paired with an '✕' close button on the top right. Below is a bold dark slate headline 'Create your account' followed by sub-copy 'Start learning in minutes.' The form features three rounded text input fields with thin gray borders containing placeholders: 'Full name', 'Email', and 'Password'. Beneath the inputs, a checkbox is paired with terms agreement copy: 'I agree to the Terms and Privacy Policy' with linked text. A prominent full-width rounded primary button in rich purple/royal blue is labeled 'Submit'. Further down, a divider with gray text reads 'or continue with', positioned above three circular outlined social authentication buttons displaying the Google 'G' icon, LinkedIn 'in' icon, and a command loop icon. The modal concludes at the bottom with a footer navigation link stating 'Already have an account? Log in'.

lead.summary: Fernway Learn presents a contemporary, clean aesthetic tailored to career-driven AI upskilling, featuring a structured landing hero and a focused registration modal. However, severe accessibility failures compromise both screens: primary CTA buttons, input placeholders, and body copy fail WCAG contrast minimums, with ratios as low as 1.48:1 and 1.80:1. Usability is further hampered by vanishing input labels, a generic 'Submit' button label, and empty skeleton wireframe cards that fail to showcase the platform's core AI tutor value proposition. Addressing these contrast deficits and replacing generic placeholders with authentic interactive course previews will significantly improve conversion and trust.

fixes.action: Increase text contrast on hero primary CTA button 'Get Started' to at least 4.5:1
fixes.why: The white text on light indigo background measures 1.95:1 (#f5feff on #a5b4fd), failing WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 and rendering the primary landing page conversion button illegible for many users.

fixes.action: Add persistent visible text labels above form inputs and increase placeholder/text contrast
fixes.why: Inputs for 'Full name', 'Email', and 'Password' lack persistent labels and measure only 1.80:1–1.81:1 (#c1c0c4 on #ffffff). Disappearing labels cause cognitive load during entry, violating WCAG 1.3.1 and 1.4.3.

fixes.action: Darken hero body copy to achieve at least 4.5:1 contrast against the pastel gradient background
fixes.why: The subhead copy measures 2.41:1 (#9b9ead on #f3f2fd), failing WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 and creating severe readability issues for prospective learners evaluating the value proposition.

fixes.action: Change the registration modal primary CTA label from 'Submit' to 'Create account'
fixes.why: 'Submit' is non-descriptive and generic; using action-oriented language clearly indicates the outcome of account creation and aligns with modern onboarding standards.

fixes.action: Replace blank skeleton lines in 'Your learning path' card with realistic curriculum milestones and AI tutor artifacts
fixes.why: The preview card displays abstract skeleton placeholder bars with empty whitespace below, failing to demonstrate tangible course outcomes, adaptive tutoring features, or career tracks.

fixes.action: Darken 'Trusted by teams' proof copy to satisfy minimum 4.5:1 text contrast
fixes.why: Text measures 1.48:1 (#d0d4d8 on #fdfefe), making social proof almost invisible to prospective users and failing WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3.

fixes.action: Increase target size and contrast for modal 'Close dialog' button
fixes.why: The close button has an estimated target size of only 12×15 CSS px (failing SC 2.5.8) and measures 2.68:1 (#9b9ea0 on #fefefe, failing SC 1.4.11), posing tap and visibility barriers.

fixes.action: Darken Terms of Service checkbox label and login footer link on registration modal
fixes.why: The legal label measures 2.64:1 (#a09ea2 on #fefefe) and login text measures 2.70:1 (#9b9ca2 on #fdfefe), both failing WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 and causing legal/navigation illegibility.

fixes.action: Replace ambiguous command loop icon with recognized OAuth provider branding and accessible labels
fixes.why: The third SSO button displays an abstract loop (⌘) rather than a recognizable provider (like GitHub or Apple), and buttons lack explicit accessible names for screen reader users.

fixes.action: Replace top-right navigation icon controls with high-contrast, labeled actions such as 'Log in'
fixes.why: The header icons measure 2.07:1 non-text contrast (#b3b3b9 on #fefefe) and fail SC 2.5.8 target size (76×16 px), while lacking visible labels or clear sign-in affordances.

fixes.action: Adjust text contrast and tap targets on header 'Courses' and 'Learn more' links
fixes.why: 'Courses' measures 4.20:1 (#797b7f on #fdfefe) and 'Learn more' measures 4.08:1 (#716ebc on #f3f3fe), falling just short of the 4.5:1 requirement.

fixes.action: Standardize hero headline typography to a uniform high-contrast color
fixes.why: Splitting the headline with periwinkle colored spans ('AI skills') follows a generic SaaS template trope that dilutes typographical hierarchy compared to weight-based emphasis.

quickWins: Update primary button copy on Screen B from 'Submit' to 'Create account'.
Darken 'Get Started' button background or text color on Screen A to meet 4.5:1 contrast.
Add persistent text labels above Full Name, Email, and Password form fields on Screen B.
Darken secondary microcopy ('Trusted by teams...', 'Start learning in minutes.', and Terms label) to satisfy WCAG AA.
Expand clickable padding on modal close button and header navigation icons to 44×44 px minimum.

visual.title: Form design
visual.text: Use single-column forms with labels above fields, group related fields, mark optional rather than required fields where most are required, use input types that match the data, and keep the primary button label specific to the outcome.

visual.title: Typography and readability
visual.text: Use a limited type scale with clear steps, body text around 16 px or larger on the web, line length of roughly 45 to 80 characters and line height around 1.4 to 1.6 for body copy. Too many sizes and weights read as disorder.

visual.title: Responsive layout
visual.text: Layouts should adapt across mobile, tablet and desktop: single column on small screens, touch targets around 44 px, no horizontal scrolling, readable maximum widths on large screens and content priority preserved when stacking.

visual.title: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1, 2.5.3 and 4.1.2 Labels and names
visual.text: Inputs need visible labels that stay visible while typing; placeholders are not labels. Icon-only buttons need an accessible name. The visible label text should be part of the accessible name.

ux.title: Form design
ux.text: Use single-column forms with labels above fields, group related fields, mark optional rather than required fields where most are required, use input types that match the data, and keep the primary button label specific to the outcome.

ux.title: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1, 2.5.3 and 4.1.2 Labels and names
ux.text: Inputs need visible labels that stay visible while typing; placeholders are not labels. Icon-only buttons need an accessible name. The visible label text should be part of the accessible name.

ux.title: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast
ux.text: Visual information needed to identify user interface components and states, such as icon buttons, input borders, focus indicators and chart elements, needs at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colours.

ux.title: Empty states
ux.text: An empty screen is an invitation to act: explain what will appear here and give one clear action to get started, rather than a blank area or a vague message.

a11y.title: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast
a11y.text: Visual information needed to identify user interface components and states, such as icon buttons, input borders, focus indicators and chart elements, needs at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colours.

a11y.title: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1, 2.5.3 and 4.1.2 Labels and names
a11y.text: Inputs need visible labels that stay visible while typing; placeholders are not labels. Icon-only buttons need an accessible name. The visible label text should be part of the accessible name.

a11y.title: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)
a11y.text: Normal text and images of text need a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against their background. Contrast ratio is (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05) where L1 and L2 are the relative luminances of the lighter and darker colours. Placeholder text and disabled-looking but active controls are frequent failures.

a11y.title: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 Large text
a11y.text: Large text needs a contrast ratio of at least 3:1. Large means at least 18 point (24 CSS px) regular, or 14 point (about 18.66 CSS px) bold. Headings that are large can use 3:1, but body copy cannot.
